content.title: About
content.content: Fonio (Digitaria exilis) is a tiny grain native to West Africa. It is considered one of the continent’s oldest cultivated cereals. The grains are small, light‑brown, and have a mild nutty flavor with a delicate texture when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fonio is often called “African quinoa” because of its high protein and nutrient content.
It is one of the fastest‑growing cereals: harvest can occur in just 6–8 weeks after sowing.
Fonio thrives in arid regions where many other crops fail.
The grains are gluten‑free, making them suitable for gluten‑free diets.
In traditional African cuisine fonio is used in couscous‑like porridges and flatbreads.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Fonio contains more protein than most common grains, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High iron content
items.content: The iron in fonio is readily absorbed and helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Provides magnesium and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for nervous system function, immunity, and metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Fonio raises blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for people managing diabetes.

items.title: Abundant dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Although rare, individual allergic reactions to fonio can occur.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking or sprouting can mitigate this.

items.title: Pesticide contamination
items.content: When purchasing, look for organic certification, especially for imported batches.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fonio can be boiled like rice, added to salads, soups, porridges, or baked into granola. Before cooking, the grains are often rinsed and soaked for 2–4 hours to shorten cooking time. It can also be milled into flour for gluten‑free baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry fonio grains in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
